newsitem.title: USA: INS criticized in California election fraud.
newsitem.headline: INS criticized in California election fraud.

text.p: The chairman of a House of Representatives committee on Monday accused the Immigration and Naturalisation Service of stalling on a request to help with the investigation of a disputed California congressional race.

House Oversight Committee William Thomas asked the INS on April 24 to match its list of naturalised citizens in Orange County, California with the list of registered voters in the 46th congressional district to help determine if illegal votes were cast in last November's election between Democrat Loretta Sanchez and Republican incumbent Bob Dornan.
Sanchez was declared the winner over Dornan by 984 votes and was sworn in as a member of the House on Jan. 7. But Dornan has charged that Sanchez won because of illegal votes by unregistered aliens.

Assistant Attorney General Andrew Fois wrote Thomas on May 1, saying it would take the INS two more weeks to determine how much information it could provide, but Thomas said that was unacceptable. The INS is part of the Justice Department.
"The INS has continued to stall in providing the committee with the information from its computer database. They're out of time," Thomas, a California Republican, said at news conference.
Thomas said the committee already had evidence of at least 300 fraudulent votes cast in the Sanchez-Dornan election.
He said if the INS would not match its database against the list of registered voters, the committee would obtain the data and do the matches on its own.
Fois said the INS wanted to help in the investigation. But he said its database was not organised for the purpose of determining eligibility to vote.
Fois said the INS also does not update its files after persons are naturalised, so women who married after they were naturalised would not be listed by their married names.
There are 1.3 million registered voters in Orange County, which includes parts of four congressional districts.
